enums.name: ke_script_reach
enums.doc: How far one instance's behaviour reaches, which is what decides whether the runtime may run a type's instances as concurrent slices.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_REACH_SELF
values.doc: Touches only the entity it is bound to. Two instances are two entities, so their work cannot overlap.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_REACH_ANY
values.doc: Reaches entities it was not handed — a borrow, a lookup by name, a query. Anything unproven belongs here: over-declaring costs parallelism, while under-declaring corrupts memory.

enums.name: ke_script_resolve
enums.doc: Why a resolve answered the way it did. Without it "no node answers" and "two nodes answer" arrive as the same invalid entity, and a binding runtime can only tell its author the borrow found nothing — sending them to look for a node that is there twice.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_RESOLVE_FOUND
values.doc: Exactly one entity answered, and it is the one returned.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_RESOLVE_NONE
values.doc: Nothing answered. The borrow names a node that is not there.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_RESOLVE_AMBIGUOUS
values.doc: More than one answered, so none was returned. Naming the borrow settles it.

enums.name: ke_script_borrow
enums.doc: Where a borrow looks for the node it names. One question asked three ways rather than three questions: a borrow is always "an instance of this type, optionally by this name", and only the region searched differs.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_BORROW_DESCENDANT
values.doc: Below the borrower, depth-first. A node reaches a grandchild it names without every level in between forwarding it.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_BORROW_ANCESTOR
values.doc: The nearest above the borrower. An ancestor chain has one node per level, so this is the one reach that can never answer ambiguous.

values.name: KE_SCRIPT_BORROW_ANYWHERE
values.doc: Anywhere the type is bound, ignoring the borrower's position. What a node reporting to a sibling subsystem needs, and the reason this is asked here rather than by a binding walking every node it knows about.

slots.name: register_type
slots.doc: Registers a script type under `name`, described by the components its instances carry and how far its behaviour reaches. Registering the same name twice returns the existing id when the description matches and fails when it does not — two languages naming one type differently would otherwise disagree about what a node in a scene file is.

slots.name: type_lookup
slots.doc: Resolves a type by name without registering it, so a scene naming a type nobody declared fails instead of inventing an empty one.

slots.name: type_components
slots.doc: The components a registered type's instances carry, in registration order. This is what a host turns into the type's query and access list, so it is read back rather than re-derived by each binding.

slots.name: type_reach
slots.doc: How far the registered type's behaviour reaches. KE_SCRIPT_REACH_ANY for an unknown id, because refusing to parallelise something unknown is the safe direction.

slots.name: bind
slots.doc: Binds `instance` to `entity` as an instance of `type`. The pointer is stored and never dereferenced. Binding an entity that already carries an instance fails rather than replacing it silently, since the previous binding's owner would then never learn its object was dropped.

slots.name: unbind
slots.doc: Drops the binding for `entity`, if any. The instance itself is the binding runtime's to release.

slots.name: instance_of
slots.doc: The instance bound to `entity`. False when none is, which is the normal answer rather than a failure: an entity a scene made without a script, or one another runtime owns, matches the same queries.

slots.name: instance_count
slots.doc: How many entities are currently bound as instances of `type`. What lets a host tell "this type had nothing to do" apart from "this type's query stopped matching", which are indistinguishable from inside the body.

slots.name: instances
slots.doc: The entities bound as instances of `type`, in binding order. What lets a binding runtime drive a type's instances without keeping a parallel list of its own — the list that only its own language can see, and that drifts from the bindings the moment anything else unbinds one. The slice belongs to the host and is invalidated by the next bind or unbind of that type, which is the same tick's structural change a caller already defers to the wave barrier.

slots.name: resolve
slots.doc: The entity `owner` borrows: an instance of `type` found within `reach`. `name` narrows it to a node of that name; empty matches on type alone, and answers ambiguous when two candidates qualify rather than picking one. `out_why` says which of the two an invalid answer was, and may be NULL.

vtables.name: ke_script_host_handle
vtables.doc: Owner wrapper: destroy releases the type table and the bindings. The instances are not touched — this host never owned them.
